title: Model ingress contract and soft-pin semantics for community weights
creator: Asha Raman
description: Clarify the acceptance criteria, metadata contract, and rollout semantics for admitting new open/community model weights into the Redwood model catalog. Introduces 'soft-pin' semantics (informational pin with automatic fallbacks) and a concise compatibility digest that runtime teams can use to determine safe serving paths.
background: We frequently onboard community/open models with varying levels of runtime compatibility. Current intake has produced intermittent production regressions due to implicit assumptions (tokenizer id mismatches, KV-cache layout differences, and quantization incompatibilities). Several PM and runtime tickets point to ambiguous pin/pinning behaviors and inconsistent compatibility notes that confuse customers and SREs. This ticket consolidates product requirements and acceptance tests so engineering can implement a deterministic ingest contract.
problem_statement: Ambiguous onboarding metadata and pin behavior cause runtime fallbacks to trigger unexpectedly, increase incident blamelogs, and make product SLAs hard to guarantee for Dedicated/Private customers. We need a precise, minimally invasive contract that prevents regressions while keeping onboarding velocity for experimental community models.
goals: Define a minimal compatibility digest schema (fields and allowed values) required for catalog admission
Specify soft-pin semantics and how they differ from hard pins (runtime, console display, and rollout behavior)
Provide clear acceptance tests (unit, integration, e2e) for model catalog ingestion and serving compatibility checks
Align stakeholders on rollout plan and observability signals to detect regressions quickly
non_goals: Exhaustively document every possible kernel-level incompatibility — that stays with runtime team
Automated model conversion tooling (out of scope for this ticket)
Changes to pricing or quota models
requirements: Catalog entry must include: model_id, variant_tag (optional), tokenizer_id, max_context_tokens (integer), preferred_quantization (enum: none, int8, fp16, q4_0, q4_1), kv_cache_support (enum: required, best_effort, none), sequence_dimension_alignment (string), model_hash (sha256), provenance_url
Compatibility digest: free-form 'compat_notes' string plus standardized flags: {kv_cache_unsafe: boolean, causal_attn_variant: enum(auto|standard|rotary|alibi), supports_streaming: boolean}

Soft-pin semantics: a catalog field 'pin_type' with values {hard, soft, unpinned}. Soft pins surface a warning in Console and allow runtime to route unless runtime has explicit incompatibility or customer required pin -> runtime should prefer hard/higher-tier pins over soft pins during capacity contention
Admission gating: models with kv_cache_support=required or kv_cache_unsafe=true must include an engineering sign-off tag and a linked runtime-compatible test PR

Automated ingest checks: a lightweight CI job that validates tokenizer_id exists in tokenizer-registry, verifies model_hash matches manifest, and runs an ingestion smoke run against a 'compat-check harness' (happy-path generation with 3 seed prompts)
Customer-visible: Console must display pin_type, compat_notes, and an estimated risk score (low/medium/high) derived from digest flags
Rollback criteria: define automatic rollback triggers if post-admit regressions exceed error thresholds (tokenization errors > 0.5% or 5xx rate increase of 3x over baseline for 30m)
acceptance_criteria: Product: Console UI shows pin_type, compat_flags, and risk_score for newly ingested model entries in staging catalog
Automated checks: ingest CI prevents merge when tokenizer_id missing or model_hash mismatch

Runtime: when a 'soft' pinned model is routed and runtime detects kv_cache_unsafe=true, runtime must either fall back to a compatible variant or return a standardized 409 with reason 'compatibility-fallback' in the logs
E2E: A staged ingress flow (QA) exercises: upload manifest -> ingest CI -> staging catalog entry -> generate prompt -> runtime returns expected token stream for all 3 seed prompts
Telemetry: post-ingest dashboard shows risk_score and vs-baseline traffic/error deltas; alerts are created when regression thresholds in requirements are met
Documentation: PRD + catalog-schema.md drafted and reviewed by Runtime and DX teams and linked from the catalog intake flow
rollout_plan: Week 0: Merge schema and ingest CI changes behind feature flag; document schema in internal Confluence
Week 1: Integrate console labels (pin_type, risk_score) in staging; create test ingest jobs for 5 community models
Week 2: Enable soft-pin enforcement for staging only; run 2-week soak with sampling of experimental models and collect telemetry
Week 3: Runtime implements fallback behaviors and standardized 409 logging; run compatibility chaos tests
Week 4: Gradual enablement to production catalog with feature-flag rollout and on-call escalation playbook
Post-rollout: 30-day review and retrospective; formalize any schema changes
dependencies: ENG-34122: compat-check harness (runtime) - must exist before ingest CI can run
DES-202: Console label/tooltip designs for 'soft-pin' and 'risk_score'
SEC-78: KMS-proof of provenance link storage (if provenance_url points to artifacts)
risks: Overly strict schema may slow onboarding of valuable experimental models (velocity vs safety trade-off)
Runtime fallback complexity could introduce performance regressions under load
Risk score heuristic may be noisy initially leading to false positives/alerts
Customers with bespoke private deployments may be incompatible with soft-pin defaults
decisions: Adopt 'soft-pin' as informational default for community models, allow customers to request hard pin via support ticket
Compatibility digest will be a small set of standardized flags plus a free-form compat_notes for edge cases
Automated ingest CI is required for admission to avoid human error and serve as first-line defense
Risk score algorithm will be simple initially (weighted flags) with plans to evolve using telemetry
